correctness.rationale: Proof checks: each isolation or six-edge gap has probability q^6; distinct locally dependent indicators have support union >=9; mixed factorial moments and cluster bounds give two independent Poisson(lambda) counts. Isolation or two unbridged gaps forces disconnection. The deterministic component-envelope trichotomy reduces all other disconnections to wrapping, tiny and intertwined patterns, bounded respectively by 3q, 3nq^10 and O(nq^7/(1-3q)); under nq^6 -> lambda all vanish. The finite code checks 53,256 support/cut assertions, while infinity is established by the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest fully inspected 2024 bounded-range-cycle paper proves the off-critical threshold and a decomposition into isolation, gap, and exceptional events but leaves the equal-exponent critical probability unspecified. The 2026 paper proves a critical law for bandwidth much larger than log n and explicitly asks about small bandwidth. The present result obtains two independent Poisson obstruction fields, a critical error estimate and e^{-2lambda}(1+lambda) at the equal-rate cubic-cycle transition. A prior analogous square-cycle theorem has a different obstruction mechanism. Historical priority beyond searched sources remains provisional.

value.rationale: The unique fixed-bandwidth resonance m=3 of obstruction exponents 2m and m(m+1)/2 is a mathematically natural boundary of small-bandwidth connectivity. The derived nontrivial critical limit e^{-2lambda}(1+lambda) and independent Poisson obstruction fields answer a concrete part of the October 2026 small-bandwidth critical-window question, in a manner that neither isolation-only nor wall-only laws capture.
